neighbours.label: clause and sentence boundaries in third-person past-tense fiction, where the story continues with 'he/she' rather than 'I': the third-person side of a narrator-person distinction (the + pole promotes 'I', 'my')
fire: She folded the letter twice and slipped it into her coat, though she knew she would read it again.
He waited by the gate for an hour. Nobody came, and the rain grew heavier.
The old man stared at the fire, though his thoughts were far away.
She had met the stranger only once, and that was years ago in Prague.
He brushed the dust from his boots. He had walked all night.
She listened at the door for a long time. The voices were quiet now.
He counted the coins again, though he already knew they were not enough.
She climbed the stairs slowly, and the old boards creaked under her.
quiet: I folded the letter twice and slipped it into my coat, though I knew I would read it again.
I waited by the gate for an hour. Nobody came, and the rain grew heavier on my hood.
I stared at the fire, though my thoughts were far away.
I had met the stranger only once, and that was years ago in Prague.
I brushed the dust from my boots. I had walked all night.
The audit found that costs rose sharply, though revenue also grew.
I counted the coins again, though I already knew they were not enough.
Sales climbed slowly in the spring, and that was mostly due to the new store.
